title: Kernel-hint orchestration for prefill/decode: attention-density probes and hedged reservations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Introduce a lightweight kernel-hint orchestration layer that probes the attention-head density and layer activation signatures at prefill time to drive (1) kernel selection choices (FP16 vs 4-bit optimized kernels, sparse attention fastpaths), and (2) an adaptive hedged-reservation policy for decode phase slots. Goal is to reduce 95th-percentile latency regressions caused by mis-selected kernels under mixed workloads while preserving throughput across high-concurrency tenants.

Background & motivation: Our current runtime picks kernels primarily based on static model profiles and observed average sequence lengths. This causes tail cases where a request with unexpectedly dense attention (long-range cross-attention or multi-document prefill) ends up using a kernel with poor memory locality, causing decode backpressure and increased prefill-to-decode handoff latency. In multi-tenant pools this amplifies head-of-line effects and fairness complaints.

Proposal:
1) Attention-density probe: add a quick, constant-time analyzer during prefill that computes a small set of metrics per request: head-density estimate (fraction of heads with non-negligible attention mass beyond local window), key-value footprint estimate, and predicted KV-cache warm-up cost. This probe runs on the CPU-side orchestrator with a tiny CPU budget (<200us typical) and returns a token indicating expected "dense" | "sparse" | "indeterminate".

2) Kernel-hint mapping: extend the model profile registry to include kernel hints tied to probe outcomes. Examples: dense -> favor full-kernel FP16 or attention-optimized kernels; sparse -> favor quantized 4-bit sparse-friendly kernels; indeterminate -> pick conservative medium-latency kernel with fallback. These hints do not force a kernel but provide a weighted preference used by the scheduler's kernel selection pass.

3) Hedged-reservation policy for decode: when a prefill probe signals dense or indeterminate and the request has low latency SLO, the scheduler will create a short-duration hedged reservation: allocate a minimal decode head slot immediately (hedge) while the full decode allocation proceeds. If allocation succeeds quickly, the hedge is released; otherwise the hedge prevents the request from being starved by long-running prefills. Hedge windows are parameterized by SLO class and can be disabled for P3 routes.

4) Fairness integration: incorporate a proportional-credit accounting adjustment where hedged reservations decrement a per-client credit bucket less aggressively than full allocations, preventing hedging from being exploited by high-frequency clients. We maintain a soft quota on simultaneous hedges per account.

Instrumentation & metrics: add new metrics and dashboards: probe_outcome_distribution, kernel_hint_chosen, hedge_inflight_count, hedge_success_rate, prefill->decode_latency_p50/p95/p99_by_probe, fairness_credit_balance. Perf experiments should record cost-per-token delta and end-to-end latency tails.

Experiment plan:
- A/B stage 1: internal-only canary on dedicated test pools with synthetic requests that vary attention density. Measure p95 latency and throughput; verify CPU probe overhead profile.
- A/B stage 2: small percentage of hosted requests (beta tenants) with full instrumentation. Monitor customer-facing errors and cost.
- Rollout: progressive traffic ramp with automated rollback if prefill->decode_p95 regresses > 10% or cost-per-token increases > 6% without commensurate latency improvements.

Implementation notes:
- Probe implementation should be model-agnostic; operate on token embeddings or attention matrices produced during prefill batch. For models where attention matrices are not available at prefill (external models), use a fast heuristic based on input length and token entropy.
- Kernel hinting requires a small schema change in model registry (hint vectors as short strings). Backwards-compatible: missing hints treated as indeterminate.
- Scheduler changes confined to agent selection pass; hedging implemented as a transient soft-slot tracked in allocation metadata.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Additional CPU overhead for probes increases infra cost; mitigate by sampling (probe only 20% of similar requests after stable signal) and enabling per-route override.
- Hedging increases short-lived allocation pressure which, if misconfigured, can worsen congestion. Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-account hedging limits, and automated telemetry-based throttles.
- Kernel misprediction still possible; we provide fast fallback path that can requeue to alternate kernel with minimal token re-emit.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 prefill->decode latency reduced by at least 12% for mixed-density workloads in testbed.
- No customer-facing error rate increase.
- Kernel hint accuracy (probe outcome matching observed kernel perf bucket) > 75% in stage 1 synthetic tests.

Rollout & operational runbook:
- Feature flag: kernel-hint-orchestrator (off by default for hosted).
- Monitor probe CPU usage and probe outcome skew.
- If hedge_success_rate < 30% or fairness_credit_balance shows hot accounts, disable hedging per-route.
- Postmortem checklist: collect representative request traces, kernel selection logs, and allocation timeline.

Related artifacts and links: Confluence design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Hint+Orchestrator, experiment dashboard (internal) https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kh/probe-experiments, prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2459, mini spec for probe metrics https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ProbeSpec.

Next steps: finalize probe feature flags and default sampling rate, implement model-registry hint schema, land probe + kernel mapper in a hidden canary, and schedule A/B stage 1 on dedicated test pools.
